title: Restriction maps between degree-zero localizations of a graded module
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be an $\mathbf N$-graded commutative ring and $M=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M_n$ a graded $S$-module ($S_kM_n\subseteq M_{k+n}$). For $f\in S$ homogeneous of positive degree let $M_f=M\otimes_SS_f$ and $M_{(f)}=\{x/f^m: m\ge0,\ x\in M_{m\deg f}\}\subseteq M_f$, a module over the ring $S_{(f)}$ (the case $M=S$) [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Let $f,g\in S$ be homogeneous of positive degree with $g^e=af$ for some $e\ge1$ and some homogeneous $a\in S$. Then: (i) $f/1$ acts invertibly on $M_g$ (inverse $a/g^e$), so there is a unique $S$-linear map $\lambda_{f,g}:M_f\to M_g$ with $\lambda_{f,g}(x/1)=x/1$ for $x\in M$; it is given by $x/f^m\mapsto a^mx/g^{em}$ (hence independent of the choice of $e,a$), it is semilinear over the ring homomorphism $\lambda^S_{f,g}:S_f\to S_g$ (the case $M=S$), and it maps $M_{(f)}$ into $M_{(g)}$; write $\rho_{f,g}:M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$ for the restriction, which is semilinear over the ring homomorphism $\rho^S_{f,g}:S_{(f)}\to S_{(g)}$. (ii) $\rho_{f,f}=\mathrm{id}$, and if $h\in S$ is homogeneous of positive degree with $h^{e'}=a'g$ ($e'\ge1$, $a'$ homogeneous), then $h^{ee'}=(a'^ea)f$ and $\rho_{g,h}\circ\rho_{f,g}=\rho_{f,h}$. (iii) Put $u=g^{\deg f}/f^{\deg g}\in S_{(f)}$. Then $\rho^S_{f,g}(u)$ is a unit of $S_{(g)}$, and $\rho_{f,g}$ induces an isomorphism of modules $\theta_{f,g}:(M_{(f)})_u\to M_{(g)}$, $(x/f^m)/u^k\mapsto\rho_{f,g}(x/f^m)\,\rho^S_{f,g}(u)^{-k}$, semilinear over the ring isomorphism $\theta^S_{f,g}:(S_{(f)})_u\to S_{(g)}$ (the case $M=S$). (iv) In the situation of (ii), with $u'=h^{\deg f}/f^{\deg h}$, the element $u$ is invertible in $(S_{(f)})_{u'}$ and $\rho_{g,h}\circ\theta_{f,g}=\theta_{f,h}\circ\kappa$, where $\kappa:(M_{(f)})_u\to(M_{(f)})_{u'}$ is the canonical localization map.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open) (1)(a),(c),(d),(e),(g),(h) and its proof (the formula $x/f^n\mapsto a^nx/g^{ne}$; 'the statements writing $S_{(g)}$ resp. $M_{(g)}$ as principal localizations of $S_{(f)}$ resp. $M_{(f)}$ are clear from the formulas above'); Algebra Section 00JL (label section-proj) for $M_{(f)}$

proof.text: *Conventions and the degenerate case.* Write $d=\deg f\ge1$, $\delta=\deg g\ge1$. All fractions are taken in $M_f$, $M_g$ (localizations of the $S$-module $M$ at the powers of $f$, resp. $g$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]: $x/g^n=0$ iff $g^kx=0$ for some $k$), and in the rings $S_f$, $S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], over which $M_f$, $M_g$ are modules by $(b/f^n)(x/f^m)=bx/f^{n+m}$. $M_{(f)}=\{x/f^m:x\in M_{md}\}$ is an $S_{(f)}$-submodule of $M_f$ ($S_{(f)}$ the ring of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]): $x/f^m+y/f^n=(f^nx+f^my)/f^{m+n}$ with $f^nx+f^my\in M_{(m+n)d}$, and $(b/f^n)(x/f^m)=bx/f^{n+m}$ with $bx\in M_{(n+m)d}$ for $b\in S_{nd}$. If $g$ is nilpotent, $g^N=0$, then $M_g=0$ (every $x/g^n=g^Nx/g^{n+N}=0$), $S_g=0$, $M_{(g)}=0$, $S_{(g)}=0$. If $g$ is not nilpotent, then $af=g^e\neq0$ is homogeneous of degree $e\delta$, and $a,f$ homogeneous with $af\ne0$ force $\deg a=e\delta-d$ (in particular $e\delta\ge d$).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: 'Write the inverse of $f$ in $S_g$ as $a/g^d$ ... $a$ homogeneous of degree $e\deg(g)-\deg(f)$'; Algebra, Section 00JM (section-proj), definition of $S_{(f)}$ and $M_{(f)}$

proof.text: *(i) The map $\lambda_{f,g}$, its formula, independence.* In $S_g$, $(f/1)(a/g^e)=af/g^e=g^e/g^e=1$, so $f/1$ is a unit of $S_g$ with inverse $a/g^e$; hence multiplication by $f$ on the $S_g$-module $M_g$ (which is multiplication by $f/1$) is bijective, with inverse multiplication by $a/g^e$. The localization map $M\to M_g$, $x\mapsto x/1$, is $S$-linear, so by the universal property of $M\to M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] (an $S$-linear map from $M$ to a module on which $f$ acts bijectively factors uniquely through $M_f$) there is a unique $S$-linear $\lambda=\lambda_{f,g}:M_f\to M_g$ with $\lambda(x/1)=x/1$. Formula: $f^m\cdot(x/f^m)=x/1$ in $M_f$, so $f^m\lambda(x/f^m)=\lambda(x/1)=x/1$ and therefore $\lambda(x/f^m)=(a/g^e)^m(x/1)=a^mx/g^{em}$. Since $\lambda$ was characterized without reference to $(e,a)$, the right-hand side is the same for every admissible pair $(e,a)$: this is the independence of the choice.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: 'For (c), the map $S_f\to S_g$ exists by (a) from the universal property of localization, or we can define it by mapping $b/f^n$ to $a^nb/g^{ne}$ ... We can similarly define $M_f\to M_g$'

proof.text: *(i) Semilinearity.* For $M=S$ step 2 gives the $S$-linear $\lambda^S=\lambda^S_{f,g}:S_f\to S_g$, $b/f^n\mapsto a^nb/g^{en}$. It is a ring homomorphism: $\lambda^S(1)=\lambda^S(1/1)=1/1$, and $\lambda^S((b/f^n)(c/f^m))=\lambda^S(bc/f^{n+m})=a^{n+m}bc/g^{e(n+m)}=(a^nb/g^{en})(a^mc/g^{em})$; additivity is $S$-linearity. $\lambda$ is $\lambda^S$-semilinear: for $s=b/f^n\in S_f$ and $z=x/f^m\in M_f$, $\lambda(sz)=\lambda(bx/f^{n+m})=a^{n+m}bx/g^{e(n+m)}=(a^nb/g^{en})(a^mx/g^{em})=\lambda^S(s)\lambda(z)$ (every element of $S_f$, $M_f$ has such a form).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: formulas $b/f^n\mapsto a^nb/g^{ne}$, $x/f^n\mapsto a^nx/g^{ne}$

proof.text: *(i) Degree zero parts; $\rho$ and $\rho^S$.* Let $x/f^m\in M_{(f)}$ with $x\in M_{md}$. If $g$ is nilpotent, $\lambda(x/f^m)\in M_g=0=M_{(g)}$ (step 1). Otherwise $\deg a=e\delta-d$ (step 1), so $a^mx\in M_{m(e\delta-d)+md}=M_{me\delta}$ and $\lambda(x/f^m)=a^mx/g^{em}\in M_{(g)}$. Thus $\lambda$ maps $M_{(f)}$ into $M_{(g)}$; let $\rho=\rho_{f,g}$ be the restriction. For $M=S$ the same computation shows that $\lambda^S$ maps the subring $S_{(f)}$ into the subring $S_{(g)}$, and the restriction $\rho^S$ is a ring homomorphism (step 3). By step 3, $\rho(rz)=\rho^S(r)\rho(z)$ for $r\in S_{(f)}$, $z\in M_{(f)}$, and $\rho$ is additive: $\rho$ is semilinear over $\rho^S$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: 'This clearly induces a map of the subrings $S_{(f)}\to S_{(g)}$ of degree zero elements as well'

proof.text: *(ii) Identity and transitivity.* For $g=f$ take $e=1$, $a=1$ ($f^1=1\cdot f$): $\rho_{f,f}(x/f^m)=1^mx/f^m=x/f^m$, so $\rho_{f,f}=\mathrm{id}$ (by independence, step 2, any other choice gives the same map). Let $h^{e'}=a'g$. Then $h^{ee'}=(a'g)^e=a'^eg^e=(a'^ea)f$ with $ee'\ge1$ and $a'^ea$ homogeneous, so $\lambda_{f,h}$, $\rho_{f,h}$ are defined. $\lambda_{g,h}\circ\lambda_{f,g}:M_f\to M_h$ is $S$-linear and sends $x/1\mapsto x/1\mapsto x/1$, so by the uniqueness in step 2 it equals $\lambda_{f,h}$; restricting to $M_{(f)}$ (step 4) gives $\rho_{g,h}\circ\rho_{f,g}=\rho_{f,h}$, and likewise $\rho^S_{g,h}\circ\rho^S_{f,g}=\rho^S_{f,h}$. Explicitly: $\rho_{g,h}(\rho_{f,g}(x/f^m))=\rho_{g,h}(a^mx/g^{em})=a'^{em}a^mx/h^{e'em}=(a'^ea)^mx/h^{ee'm}$, the formula of $\rho_{f,h}$ for the pair $(ee',a'^ea)$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: formula $x/f^n\mapsto a^nx/g^{ne}$; Constructions, Section 01M3 after Definition 01M5: 'canonical maps $M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$ and $M_{(g)}\to M_{(f)}$ which are mutually inverse'

proof.text: *(iii) $u\in S_{(f)}$ and $\rho^S(u)$ is a unit.* $g^d\in S_{\delta d}=S_{d\delta}$, so $u=g^d/f^\delta\in S_{(f)}$, and $v=f^\delta/g^d\in S_{(g)}$ ($f^\delta\in S_{d\delta}$). Since $\lambda^S$ is a ring homomorphism with $\lambda^S(f/1)=f/1$ and $\lambda^S(g/1)=g/1$, and $u\cdot(f/1)^\delta=g^d/1$ in $S_f$, we get $\rho^S(u)\,(f/1)^\delta=g^d/1$ in $S_g$, hence $\rho^S(u)\cdot v=\rho^S(u)(f/1)^\delta\cdot(1/g^d)=g^d/g^d=1$. So $\rho^S(u)$ is a unit of $S_{(g)}$ with inverse $v=f^\delta/g^d$. (In $S_g$, $\rho^S(u)=a^\delta g^d/g^{e\delta}$; the inverse is $v$, not a fraction with $a$ in the denominator.)

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: clause (a): '$f^{\deg(g)}/g^{\deg(f)}$ is invertible in $S_{(g)}$' (Stacks proves it via primes; here by the formula, as the proof's 'clear from the formulas' allows)

proof.text: *(iii) The map $\theta$.* Regard $M_{(g)}$ as an $S_{(f)}$-module through $\rho^S$; by step 4, $\rho:M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$ is $S_{(f)}$-linear, and $u$ acts on $M_{(g)}$ as multiplication by the unit $\rho^S(u)$ (step 6), i.e. bijectively. By the universal property of the localization $(M_{(f)})_u$ of the $S_{(f)}$-module $M_{(f)}$ at $u$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] there is a unique $S_{(f)}$-linear $\theta=\theta_{f,g}:(M_{(f)})_u\to M_{(g)}$ with $\theta(z/1)=\rho(z)$; as in step 2, $u^k\cdot(z/u^k)=z/1$ forces $\theta(z/u^k)=\rho^S(u)^{-k}\rho(z)$. For $M=S$ this gives $\theta^S:(S_{(f)})_u\to S_{(g)}$, $r/u^k\mapsto\rho^S(u)^{-k}\rho^S(r)$, a ring homomorphism: $\theta^S(1)=1$ and $\theta^S((r/u^j)(r'/u^k))=\rho^S(u)^{-j-k}\rho^S(rr')=\theta^S(r/u^j)\theta^S(r'/u^k)$ ($\rho^S$ multiplicative). $\theta$ is $\theta^S$-semilinear: $\theta((r/u^j)(z/u^k))=\theta(rz/u^{j+k})=\rho^S(u)^{-j-k}\rho^S(r)\rho(z)=\theta^S(r/u^j)\theta(z/u^k)$ (step 4).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: clauses (e),(h): 'the map $M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$ induces an isomorphism $(M_{(f)})_{g^{\deg(f)}/f^{\deg(g)}}\cong M_{(g)}$'

proof.text: *(iii) $\theta$ is surjective.* Let $y/g^n\in M_{(g)}$, $y\in M_{n\delta}$. Put $Y=g^{n(d-1)}y\in M_{n\delta+n(d-1)\delta}=M_{nd\delta}$ (here $d\ge1$); then $y/g^n=Y/g^{nd}$ in $M_g$, and $z=Y/f^{n\delta}\in M_{(f)}$ since $Y\in M_{(n\delta)d}$. Compute in $M_g$, where $f/1$ is a unit (step 2): $\rho(z)=\lambda(Y/f^{n\delta})=(f/1)^{-n\delta}(Y/1)$ and $\rho^S(u)^{-n}=v^n=(f/1)^{n\delta}/g^{nd}$ (step 6). Hence $\theta(z/u^n)=\rho^S(u)^{-n}\rho(z)=(f/1)^{n\delta}(1/g^{nd})(f/1)^{-n\delta}(Y/1)=Y/g^{nd}=y/g^n$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: 'clear from the formulas above' (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *(iii) $\theta$ is injective, hence an isomorphism.* Let $\theta(z/u^k)=0$ with $z=x/f^m$, $x\in M_{md}$. Multiplying by $\rho^S(u)^k$ gives $\rho(z)=0$, i.e. $a^mx/g^{em}=0$ in $M_g$, so $g^Na^mx=0$ in $M$ for some $N\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Multiply by $f^m$: $g^{N+em}x=g^N(af)^mx=f^m\cdot g^Na^mx=0$. Choose $K$ with $Kd\ge N+em$; then $g^{Kd}x=0$, so $u^K z=g^{Kd}x/f^{K\delta+m}=0$ in $M_f$, hence in $M_{(f)}$, and therefore $z/u^k=0$ in $(M_{(f)})_u$ (an element $z/u^k$ vanishes when a power of $u$ kills $z$). So $\theta$ is bijective; being additive and $\theta^S$-semilinear, it is an isomorphism of modules over the ring map $\theta^S$, and for $M=S$, $\theta^S$ is a bijective ring homomorphism, a ring isomorphism. This is (iii).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), proof: 'clear from the formulas above' (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *(iv) Compatibility with transitivity and the localization maps.* Let $h^{e'}=a'g$ as in (ii), so $h^{ee'}=(a'^ea)f$ and (iii) applies to the pair $(f,h)$ with the element $u'=h^d/f^{\deg h}$, giving the ring isomorphism $\theta^S_{f,h}:(S_{(f)})_{u'}\to S_{(h)}$ and $\theta_{f,h}$. $u$ is invertible in $(S_{(f)})_{u'}$: $\theta^S_{f,h}(u/1)=\rho^S_{f,h}(u)=\rho^S_{g,h}(\rho^S_{f,g}(u))$ (step 5) is the image of the unit $\rho^S_{f,g}(u)$ (step 6) under a ring homomorphism, hence a unit, and $\theta^S_{f,h}$ is a ring isomorphism, so $u/1$ is a unit. Hence the canonical $S_{(f)}$-linear map $\kappa:(M_{(f)})_u\to(M_{(f)})_{u'}$ with $\kappa(z/1)=z/1$ exists [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] (universal property, $u$ acting bijectively on $(M_{(f)})_{u'}$ through the unit $u/1$), $\kappa(z/u^k)=(u/1)^{-k}(z/1)$. For $z\in M_{(f)}$: $\rho_{g,h}(\theta_{f,g}(z/u^k))=\rho_{g,h}(\rho^S_{f,g}(u)^{-k}\rho_{f,g}(z))=\rho^S_{f,h}(u)^{-k}\rho_{f,h}(z)$ (step 4: $\rho_{g,h}$ is $\rho^S_{g,h}$-semilinear and $\rho^S_{g,h}$ preserves inverses of units; step 5), and $\theta_{f,h}(\kappa(z/u^k))=\theta^S_{f,h}(u/1)^{-k}\theta_{f,h}(z/1)=\rho^S_{f,h}(u)^{-k}\rho_{f,h}(z)$ (step 7 for $(f,h)$). So $\rho_{g,h}\circ\theta_{f,g}=\theta_{f,h}\circ\kappa$; likewise for $M=S$ (with $\rho^S$, $\theta^S$). The special case $g=f$ ($e=1,a=1$, $u=f^d/f^d=1$, $(M_{(f)})_1=M_{(f)}$, $\theta_{f,f}=\mathrm{id}$ by steps 5, 7) says that $\theta_{f,h}$ carries the canonical map $M_{(f)}\to(M_{(f)})_{u'}$ to $\rho_{f,h}$. This is (iv).
